source.paper: arXiv:2509.23162v1 (the revision judged at HF head 5d96031f01d2b0e83e0e8cbdd3ad9baadb26ce45)

statement: For N=1000 non-commuting Gaussian patterns in d=10, Algorithm 1 converges in one step at beta=1 for radii 1/sqrt(beta N) and 100/sqrt(beta N), with higher variance and an approximately 1e-3 error floor; beta=0.1 does not converge.
falsification_acceptance: Every memory has mean norm squared d, covariance trace d, and a positive-definite covariance generated from WW^T+0.01I.
The covariance family is numerically non-commuting.
Every query has the requested W2 radius, with half the squared budget in its mean and half in its covariance.
At beta=1, the lower endpoint of every one-step mean-error 95% interval exceeds the paper's 1e-3 level.
At beta=1 and radius 100/sqrt(N), the lower endpoint exceeds 0.1 after one update and 0.05 after five updates.
The hash-pinned v1 Figure 8 panel (b) independently digitizes above 0.1 after one update and 0.05 after five.
A second valid random-PSD law (rank-one directions) also has a one-step lower confidence bound above 0.1 at the 100x radius.
At beta=0.1, both radii have at most 1% of queries below the 1e-3 prose threshold.
A SciPy square-root loop independently matches the batched Algorithm 1 update.
A beta-zero uniform-weight lower bound rules out retrieval.
verdict_rule: FALSIFIED only if every scale, assumption, checker, control, and contradiction check passes; otherwise BLOCKED.
